time_weight_source: src/smart/diffusion/component_loss.py:85, t_eps=.05, w_p=clamp(t,.05)^(-p)/E[clamp(t,.05)^(-p)], uniform t; small t is close to clean data
train_manifest_note: Main continuations store the remaining-manifest hash while fresh targeted runs store full-manifest hash; paired full train_order hashes are identical. Continuation state/order audit is separate; no bitwise CUDA-equivalence claim.
histogram_limit: Midpoint estimates over official histogram bins, not exact raw-sample moments. First speed bin is0–1m/s, not an exact stationary fraction.

selection.selection_rule: Preserve legacy and warm_winner; choose two lowest EMA S new recipes subject to generated_onroad_fraction >=0.72 and generated/GT vehicle count within [0.8,1.2]. Gate is only a minimum-quality check, not converged quality.

findings.finding: MSE-heading widthp2 improves4096EMA composite at both heading powers; headingp2 alone does not improve angular or composite performance.
findings.limit: Single paired seed and budget. Warm and width-only composite differ .000831, no statistical winner.

findings.finding: Changing heading kind from angleMSE to angleL1 at fixedp1/weight1 lowers angularJSD ~71% for both width powers.
findings.hypothesis: AngleL1 has constant residual-gradient magnitude away from its cusp; angleMSE scales gradient with|angularerror|. L1 may reduce domination by ambiguous large-error heading examples, improving the generated angular distribution. Both are circular-angle losses, so this is not a vector-MSE180deg-gradient explanation.
findings.limit: No claim that L1 recovers every mode or the full128-epoch optimum.

findings.finding: The selected L1-heading+widthp2 recipe is not the best standalone width recipe.
findings.hypothesis: Power changes alter which time regions teach a shared denoiser; effects couple to position, heading, sizes, Hungarian correspondence and collision. Composite improvement does not imply the targeted marginal improves.

findings.finding: The strongposMSE32/col20/headL1/shape2 joint recipe wins current4096EMA S, primarily from angular improvement against its parent.
findings.limit: Heading kindMSE→L1,headingweight.25→1 and bothsizeweights1→2 change together. Cannot infer that doubling shape weights helped, or attribute the total result to heading kind alone.

findings.finding: Time normalization equalizes E[w], not E[wL(t)] or gradient scale.
findings.support: Tail256 width weighted-loss median .099984→.024724 underp1→p2 in the L1-head pair; normalizedp2 concentrates76.9% of weight belowt=.1 versus42.4% forp1.
findings.hypothesis: Residuals are lower near clean data; emphasizing those times can decrease actual average weighted contribution despite unchanged numerical componentweight.

findings.finding: Weights interact through shared gradients and frequent clipping.
findings.support: All256 tail updates exceedclip=.5 for the five inspected recipes; preclip medians3.32 for L1head,7.72 for jointstronggeo/shape2 versus6.17 parent.
findings.limit: Loss values and total gradient norms do not decompose per-component gradient directions or prove which component caused a metric change.

findings.finding: Shapes retain narrower generated distributions and speed remains underrepresented in their tails despite low JSD.
findings.limit: Binned estimates and generatedvehicle-type composition confound these moments; low aggregateJSD is not exact physical-distribution equality.

freeze_and_confirmation: Selection matches the fixed road≥.72/count.8–1.2 gate, preservinglegacy/warm and addingjointstronggeo+L1W2. Freeze recipe expansion; await6144 actual results, originalbatch512 freshmulti-epoch and independent-seed/heldout confirmation. No numeric128-epoch extrapolation.
